deleteAccount.title: Delete your account for good
deleteAccount.whatAccount: Your account and all personal data in it are deleted.
deleteAccount.whatOrganization: Your organization {name} is deleted with all its data, including uploaded files.
deleteAccount.whatLicenceMoneyBack: Your paid licence is cancelled first. You are within the 30 days money back: a credit note cancels the invoice and comes by email. If you have already paid, we transfer the amount back to you within 30 days of the cancellation.
deleteAccount.whatLicenceRenewal: Your paid licence is cancelled first and does not renew. The invoice for the current year stands, and nothing is refunded.
deleteAccount.whatEmail: The erasure confirmation then goes to {email}.
deleteAccount.whatInvoices: Invoices and credit notes already issued stay on record for as long as tax law requires (§ 147 AO, § 14b UStG). An invoice that is not cancelled stays payable.
deleteAccount.confirmLabel: Type your email address to confirm:
deleteAccount.failed: The account could not be deleted just now. Please try again later or write to contact@nisd2.eu.

refused.reauth: To be safe, please sign in again before deleting your account. You come back here afterwards.
refused.platform_admin: Platform admins cannot delete their account here.
refused.several_organizations: You own several organizations. Write to contact@nisd2.eu and we will delete the account with you.
refused.pays_for_others: Your billing account also pays for another organization, which would be left without anyone who can pay. Write to contact@nisd2.eu and we will sort it out with you.
refused.order_check: An order on your account is still being checked. Write to contact@nisd2.eu and we will delete the account once it is settled.
refused.cancel_first: Your paid licence could not be cancelled together with the account. Cancel it under Billing, then delete the account here.
refused.cancel_failed: Your paid licence could not be cancelled just now, so nothing was deleted. Please try again later or write to contact@nisd2.eu.
refused.cancel_unclear: We could not confirm whether your licence was cancelled, so nothing was deleted. We are checking it now. Please do not try again: write to contact@nisd2.eu and we will delete the account once it is settled.
refused.cancel_by_us: Your paid licence is still running and can still be cancelled. Write to contact@nisd2.eu and we will cancel it and delete the account with you.
refused.billing_busy: An order or cancellation is being processed on your account right now. Please try again in a minute.
refused.other_members: Your organization has other members, and deleting your account would delete the organization with their work. Remove the other members first, or write to contact@nisd2.eu.

assets.text: This is what your asset register looks like: the software, devices and services your company works with. In the NIS 2 walkthrough you enter them step by step.

suppliers.text: This is what your supplier list looks like: who works for you and how much your operations depend on them. The walkthrough fills it from your assets.

risks.text: This is what your risk register looks like: every asset and supplier with its level in the risk matrix and what you do about it.

policies.text: This is what your documents look like: the policy, plans and concepts the walkthrough writes with you, approved by your management in the app.

training.text: This is what your trainings look like: who learned what and when, the management body training included.
rows: USB sticks and remote maintenance on the machines

managementReviews.text: This is what your management reviews look like: when management checked the implementation and what it decided.
rows: Policy and incident plan approved. Second factor for the ERP by 31 March 2027.

journeyNotice.title: The journey is the detailed view. Go there anyway?
journeyNotice.text: It shows every requirement at once, with the registers that go with them. We recommend this view for large companies (250 employees or more, as the EU defines them) with their own information security team. For everyone else we recommend the NIS 2 walkthrough: it takes you through item by item and explains each step.

hero.title: Your NIS2 implementation
hero.subtitle: {done} of {total} records are in place. Most build themselves from your work; you review and sign off.

path.title: The whole path
path.hint: Every measure. Switch between Critical first (our recommendation) and Chronological (the natural order).

view.criticalTip: Biggest risk and liability first. Our recommendation.
view.chronoTip: In the natural order of the process, the way it is usually worked through.

coverage.doneTip: Implemented and documented. Stays current with little effort.
coverage.currentTip: Your next step. One click and you move on.
coverage.preparedTip: We drafted it for you. You review and sign off instead of starting from scratch.
coverage.openTip: Not started yet. Comes up once the steps before it are in place.
coverage.overdueTip: A recurring task is due, such as an annual refresh. A quick update.

owner.leadershipResp: Approves and owns it. Governance, budget and the duties under § 38 BSIG.
owner.securityResp: Runs risk, incidents, access, training and effectiveness.
owner.itResp: Implements the technical measures: cryptography, patches, authentication.
owner.operationsResp: Owns continuity, backups and supplier management.

band.minimumHint: The mandatory, foundational measures. The base that has to stand first.
band.yearHint: About two hours a week. Not a sprint, a calm rhythm.
band.laterHint: Once the rest is in place. Important, but not urgent.
